claims.claim: **Infantile spasms are sudden, brief, bilateral, symmetric contractions of the neck, trunk and limbs, occurring in clusters.** They often belong to one of the commonest severe infant epilepsy syndromes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Prompt diagnosis and treatment are critical to limit developmental harm** — over 80% have developmental delay, with high rates of ongoing epilepsy.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Peak onset 3–7 months, but any age in childhood.** Most have Infantile Epileptic Spasms Syndrome: spasms, hypsarrhythmia on EEG and developmental arrest or regression (formerly West syndrome).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suggestive features:** clusters, usually shortly after waking; abrupt whole-body spasms, flexor or extensor; **may be subtle — head nodding or facial/ocular movements**, especially early; usually but not always symmetric. **Ask parents to record episodes.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Differentials:** other infantile epilepsies, benign myoclonic epilepsy of infancy, and non-epileptic episodes (sleep myoclonus, shuddering, Sandifer syndrome).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Common causes:** trisomy 21, tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC), perinatal hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy, focal structural abnormalities.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Clues:** a known associated condition; family history of seizures or delay; **early handedness** (focal lesion); dysmorphism; **hypopigmented macules** (TSC); pre-existing delay; neonatal or early infantile seizures; rapidly increasing head circumference.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Early neurological consultation for every suspected case.** Strongly consider admission where it will speed investigations and treatment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **EEG awake and asleep, urgently; MRI brain promptly**; if the cause is unknown, genetic testing and a urine metabolic screen.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer if urgent EEG, prompt MRI and neurology consultation aren't available locally.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treatment is always neurologist-led. High-dose prednisolone is first line** — except in TSC and treatable metabolic conditions. Dose and weaning are set by the neurologist.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prednisolone + vigabatrin stops spasms more often than prednisolone alone, but showed no better development at 18 months.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **High-dose prednisolone raises the risk of serious infection and adrenal crisis.** Every child needs a **steroid alert card and a sick day management plan.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Febrile or unwell → manage as high-risk under the sepsis guidelines** (immunocompromised). **Vomiting or significant diarrhoea → give IV/IM hydrocortisone** (adrenal insufficiency risk).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **While on prednisolone:** check weight, glucose and blood pressure twice a week; consider a PPI and prophylactic trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Delay vaccines until one month after ceasing prednisolone**; consider nirsevimab per local guidelines given the degree of immunosuppression.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Admission is usually brief, and discharge does not depend on spasms stopping.** Arrange paediatric neurology follow-up and **a follow-up EEG, ideally two weeks after starting treatment.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give parents the steroid alert card and an individualised sick day plan before discharge.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23
